# 2 Samuel Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 173r–174r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_006_page_001.jpg, 2SA_006_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand. **2** David arose and went with all the people from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name — the name of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim.

**3** They set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart. **4** They brought it from the house of Abinadab on the hill, accompanying the ark of God, and Ahio walked before the ark.

**5** David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all manner of instruments of cypress wood — with lyres, harps, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.

**6** When they came to the threshing floor of Nachon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen had stumbled. **7** The anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his error, and he died there beside the ark of God.

**8** David was angry that the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day. **9** David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"

**10** David was not willing to bring the ark of the LORD to the City of David, so he diverted it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. **11** The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

**12** When King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God," David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.

**13** When those who bore the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fatted calf. **14** David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod. **15** David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.

**16** As the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.

**17** They brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

**18** When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts. **19** He distributed to all the people, the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, to each one a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake. Then all the people departed, each to his house.

**20** David returned to bless his household. But Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel honored himself today — uncovering himself before the eyes of his servants' maidservants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"

**21** David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD — who chose me over your father and over all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel — I will celebrate before the LORD!

**22** I will make myself even more lowly than this, and I will be humble in my own eyes. But by the maidservants of whom you have spoken, I shall be held in honor."

**23** And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter's dramatic arc: the first attempt to bring the ark (vv.1-5), the disaster at Nachon's threshing floor (vv.6-10), the successful second attempt (vv.11-19), and the confrontation with Michal (vv.20-23). The theological tension between joy and danger in YHWH's presence is consistently rendered.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.5 — "playing" vs. "celebrating" vs. "dancing wildly"
- **EMET:** "playing [mesachaqim]"
- **LOGOS:** "celebrating"
- **PNEUMA:** "dancing wildly"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "celebrating" — captures the festive context. EMET's "playing" is too ambiguous; PNEUMA's "wildly" adds intensity not in the text.

### V.7 — "error" vs. "offense"
- **EMET:** "the-error [shal]" / **LOGOS:** "his error" / **PNEUMA:** "his offense"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his error" — *shal* is a hapax legomenon; "error" is more neutral than "offense."

### V.8 — "burned to David" vs. "was angry" vs. "was furious"
- **EMET:** "it-burned to-David"
- **LOGOS:** "David was angry"
- **PNEUMA:** "David was furious"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "David was angry" — *charah* means anger was kindled. PNEUMA's "furious" escalates beyond the text.

### V.14 — "whirling with all strength" vs. "danced with all his might" vs. "wearing nothing but"
- **EMET:** "whirling [mekharker] with-all strength"
- **LOGOS:** "danced before the LORD with all his might"
- **PNEUMA:** "danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing nothing but a linen ephod"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod." PNEUMA's "nothing but" adds emphasis not in the text — the Hebrew simply says *David chagur efod bad* (David was girded with a linen ephod).

### V.19 — *eshpar* (hapax)
- **EMET:** "one portion [eshpar]"
- **LOGOS:** "a portion of meat"
- **PNEUMA:** "a portion of dates"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a portion of meat" — the traditional rendering based on Aramaic/Syriac cognates. PNEUMA's "dates" is a viable alternative but less well-supported.

### V.20 — "empty ones" vs. "vulgar fellows" vs. "common exhibitionist"
- **EMET:** "the-empty-ones [reyqim]"
- **LOGOS:** "vulgar fellows"
- **PNEUMA:** "some common exhibitionist"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "vulgar fellows" — LOGOS captures the social contempt of *reyqim*. PNEUMA's "exhibitionist" is too modern.

### V.22 — "lightly esteemed" vs. "lowly" vs. "foolish"
- **EMET:** "lightly-esteemed [niqalotiy]"
- **LOGOS:** "more contemptible" → "I will make myself even more contemptible"
- **PNEUMA:** "even lower... look foolish"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "more lowly" — *niqalotiy* from the root *qalal* (to be light/despised). "Lowly" captures the self-humbling aspect; "contemptible" (LOGOS) is too harsh for what David intends.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
